newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy Q4 GDP seen shrinking 0.1 pct q/q.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy Q4 GDP seen shrinking 0.1 pct q/q.

text.p: Italy's economy is likely to have shrunk 0.1 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 compared to Q3 but should have risen 0.5 percent year-on-year, a Reuter poll of analysts showed.

Preliminary GDP data are due to be released on Friday and forecasts for quarter-on-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) range from down 0.5 percent to up 0.2 percent for an average decline of 0.1 percent.
Many analysts revised down their forecast for Q4 GDP after December industrial production data which fell an unexpected 3.1 percent year-on-year and 1.7 percent on average in 1996.
Zero GDP growth in Q4 would bring 1996 average growth to 0.8 percent, in line with the last government forecasts for 1997, Italian bank Cariplo said in a newsletter.

JP Morgan, which forecasts zero growth to a 0.1 percent rise quarter on quarter, said in a research note that as well as weak industrial production in Q4, fewer working days also went in the quarter's disfavour compared with Q3.
"Private consumption and equipment investment is likely to have fallen over the previous quarter...while a small contribution could have come from inventories," JP Morgan added.

Paolo Casadio, analyst at Credito Italiano said the proposed 1997 mini-budget and uncertainty over European economic and monetary union (EMU) had a psychological impact on "consumption and investment causing short term deviations of these components from the expected trajectory based on economic fundementals."
Credito Italiano saw no impact from inventories, while foreign demand continued to show "weak support but declining from the previous quarter."
Lucia Trevisan, analyst at Caboto, said: "Private consumption was unchanged while public consumption contracted. None of the components in internal demand supports growth."
On the trade balance, she said: "Exports are rising only a bit but imports are falling, so the net effect is positive."
The Q4 data should "confirm a weak economic picture characterised by weak internal demand both in terms of consumption and investments," Paolo Pizzoli, economist at Banca Akros said.
Furthermore in Q4 "the inventory build-up, which should resume in 1997, had not yet started," he said.
The contribution from the construction sector would be lower as would that from exports, while investment would remain weak, according to San Paolo economists.
In addition, San Paolo said: "If Q4 growth for 1996 is low, 1997 growth has a lower base to start from and therefore can't reach a high rate."
On 1997 growth the supply side is starting to show some sign of pick-up after negative sentiment previously but that pick-up will take time to filter to industrial production and GDP.
"However this is a promise of higher growth later on in 1997," San Paolo said.

National statistics body Istat will publish the preliminary figure on Friday. Final data, subdivided by sector, will be released on April 14, when Istat will also publish the annual revision on the 1996 data.
